meta.project: Multilingual, Ontology-Aware, and Explainable ESG Intelligence System
meta.description: Integrated research traceability matrix mapping ESG objective layers to technical contributions and empirical literature evidence.

research_questions: RQ1.1: How can Transformer-based architectures be optimized for bilingual ESG ABSA?
RQ1.3: How can regional calibration and ESG lexicons mitigate bias?

literature_references.title: Can You Translate for Me? Code-Switched Machine Translation with Large Language Models
literature_references.authors: Jyotsana Khatri, Vivek Srivastava, L. Vig
literature_references.relevance: Supports C3 and RQ1.1 by evaluating LLM performance in code-switched multilingual communities, highlighting factual inconsistencies and gender bias that must be mitigated in bilingual ESG platforms.

literature_references.title: Single Ground Truth Is Not Enough: Adding Flexibility to Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis Evaluation
literature_references.relevance: Establishes the empirical necessity for C1 and C2 by demonstrating that traditional single-ground-truth ABSA evaluation misrepresents accuracy in subjective domains, advocating for flexible span extraction.

contributions: C8: Large-scale ESG LLM benchmark (30+ models)
research_questions: RQ2.1: To what extent does few-shot learning improve ESG granularity?
RQ2.2: How can long-context mechanisms enhance scalability?
RQ2.4: How can multi-LLM fusion reduce hallucination?

literature_references.title: HMT: Hierarchical Memory Transformer for Efficient Long Context Language Processing
literature_references.relevance: Directly justifies C13 and RQ2.2 by proposing a memory-augmented segment-level recurrence that enables long-document processing with 2.5–116x less inference memory.

literature_references.title: Ensembling Large Language Models with Process Reward-Guided Tree Search for Better Complex Reasoning
literature_references.relevance: Supports C10 and RQ2.4 by providing a framework (LE-MCTS) for ensembling language models to identify the most accurate reasoning chain through tree search.

research_questions: RQ3.1: How can symbolic reasoning be integrated using ESG ontologies?
RQ3.2: How can transparent outputs be ensured via reasoning graphs?
RQ3.3: How can implicit ESG claims be identified?

literature_references.title: Verify-in-the-Graph: Entity Disambiguation Enhancement for Complex Claim Verification with Interactive Graph Representation
literature_references.relevance: Provides causal evidence for C7 and RQ3.2, illustrating how structured triplet decomposition and knowledge-base interaction resolve ambiguous entities for deep sub-claim verification.

literature_references.title: Verifiable by Design: Aligning Language Models to Quote from Pre-Training Data
literature_references.relevance: Supports C15 and RQ3.2 by introducing Quote-Tuning, a method to enhance verifiability through verbatim attribution, essential for audit-ready explainability.

research_questions: RQ4.1: How can XAI improve stakeholder trust in ESG outputs?
RQ4.5: Can tone–outcome mismatch reliably indicate greenwashing?

literature_references.title: Towards Knowledge Checking in Retrieval-augmented Generation: A Representation Perspective
literature_references.relevance: Supports C11 and RQ4.5 by demonstrating how representation-based classifiers can identify misleading information in RAG systems, providing a foundation for mismatch detection.

literature_references.title: On the Impact of Fine-Tuning on Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
literature_references.relevance: Justifies the need for C14 and RQ4.1 by showing that fine-tuning can decrease the faithfulness of CoT reasoning, requiring explicit tone-aware bias correction.

research_questions: RQ5.1: How can transparent and auditable outputs be ensured?
RQ5.2: How can reasoning quality and consistency be operationalized at scale?

literature_references.title: MICE for CATs: Model-Internal Confidence Estimation for Calibrating Agents with Tools
literature_references.relevance: Supports C1 and RQ5.1 by introducing a class of confidence estimators that allow agents to weigh risk versus reward, ensuring auditable decision processes during deployment.

literature_references.title: A Survey of QUD Models for Discourse Processing
literature_references.relevance: Justifies C12 and O5 by reviewing Question Under Discussion (QUD) frameworks, providing a linguistic foundation for the interactive dashboard communication strategies.
